primitives.name: Test Set Contamination
primitives.verbatim_quote: Benchmarks are typically published on the internet, and most modern LLMs include large swaths of the internet in their training data.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P(contamination)': 'Dimensionless probability of test set contamination', 'Benchmark Size': 'Number of unique evaluation samples', 'Evaluation Frequency': 'Times per year a model is tested against the benchmark', 'Internet Growth Rate': 'Annual rate of increase in total internet content volume'}
primitives.assumptions: Assumes uniform distribution of benchmark data across the internet and independent sampling during training.
primitives.breakdown_regime: As Internet Growth Rate → 0, P(contamination) → ∞, leading to benchmark obsolescence.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI conformal prediction intervals for model performance under covariate shift, where contaminated benchmarks create biased empirical cumulative distribution functions.
layer2.telemetry: Drop in accuracy when evaluating on previously unseen internet snapshots.

primitives.name: Automatic Ground-Truth Scoring
primitives.verbatim_quote: We release LiveBench, the first benchmark that (1) contains frequently-updated questions from recent information sources, (2) scores answers automatically according to objective ground-truth values, and (3) contains a wide variety of challenging tasks, spanning math, coding, reasoning, language, instruction following, and data analysis.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Score': 'Dimensionless accuracy score (0 ≤ Score ≤ 1)', 'N': 'Total number of questions', 'y_i^{model}': "Model's answer to question i", 'y_i^{ground}': 'Objective ground-truth answer to question i', '\\mathbb{I}(\\cdot)': 'Indicator function returning 1 if condition holds, else 0'}
primitives.assumptions: Assumes ground truth is deterministic, error-free, and fully captures the desired answer semantics.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When ground truth is ambiguous or changes over time, automatic scoring becomes unreliable.

layer2.mapping: Reduces to GSE state-transition mapping where the system's next state is determined by an automated verifier checking compliance with formal specifications, avoiding human bias.
layer2.telemetry: Consistency of scoring metrics across repeated evaluations of identical answers.

primitives.name: Monthly Updates
primitives.verbatim_quote: Questions are added and updated on a monthly basis, and we release new tasks and harder versions of tasks over time so that LiveBench can distinguish between the capabilities of LLMs as they improve in the future.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Q(t)': 'Total number of questions at time t', 'Q_0': 'Initial number of questions', '\\lambda': 'Monthly growth rate of new questions', 't': 'Time in months since launch'}
primitives.assumptions: Exponential growth assumes constant discovery rate of new challenging questions and no saturation effect.
primitives.breakdown_regime: As t → ∞, the update frequency becomes impractical due to diminishing returns in difficulty.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI epistemic uncertainty quantification where the credible region shrinks with each new observation, reflecting increased confidence but also potential overfitting to recent data.
layer2.telemetry: Rate of change in average question difficulty over rolling 3-month windows.

primitives.name: Contamination-Limited Tasks
primitives.verbatim_quote: To achieve this, LiveBench contains questions that are based on recently-released math competitions, arXiv papers, news articles, and datasets, and it contains harder, contamination-limited versions of tasks from previous benchmarks such as Big-Bench Hard, AMPS, and IFEval.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'T_{cl}': 'Contamination-limited task instance', 'T_{raw}': 'Original task from raw dataset', 'H_{recent}': 'Set of recently released sources (news, papers)', 'f(\\cdot, \\cdot)': 'Filtering function ensuring minimal overlap with training corpora'}
primitives.assumptions: Assumes recentness is a proxy for novelty, ignoring temporal smoothing effects in data collection.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When H_{recent} saturates, T_{cl} approaches standard benchmarks, losing contamination resistance.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE adversarial robustness testing where contamination-limited tasks serve as perturbed inputs to evaluate worst-case performance, avoiding benign accuracy artifacts.
layer2.telemetry: Proportion of training tokens shared between benchmark updates and model pre-training corpora.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge is separating signal from noise in model evaluation. Standard benchmarks suffer from 'data bleed' where test sets become part of the training distribution, creating circularity. LiveBench introduces automatic ground-truth scoring to eliminate subjective LLM or human judges, who introduce biases and fail on hard questions. However, automatic scoring requires robust definitions of 'correctness', which may not capture nuanced understanding. The monthly updates ensure tasks remain fresh, but exponential growth risks overfitting to recent trends rather than general principles. Contamination-limited tasks force models to reason from first principles rather than memorizing patterns. Together, these primitives form a rigorous, adaptive framework that measures progress while guarding against common pitfalls, enabling fair comparisons as models scale.
